scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

Scenario:
AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw:
I would say: 1

You are the one who is in the wrong in this situation. While it's understandable that you need help with transportation for your son, it's not fair to expect your boyfriend to take on this responsibility, especially considering his already demanding work schedule. 

You asked him to pick up and drop off your son on weekends, which would require him to adjust his own plans and schedule. When he expressed his discomfort and declined, you snapped at him and guilt-tripped him into feeling like he's not committed to your family. 

It's also important to note that your boyfriend has been supporting you and your son financially, and it's reasonable for him to want to use his weekends for his own relaxation and leisure activities. 

By suggesting that he's not a part of your family if he doesn't agree to help with transportation, you're putting undue pressure on him and making him feel like he's being forced into a role he's not ready for. 

It's not about being "part of the family" or not, but about respecting each other's boundaries and priorities. Your boyfriend's suggestion to break up may seem extreme, but it's clear that he feels overwhelmed and undervalued in the relationship. 

Your reaction to his concerns, telling him to "welcome to the real world," comes across as dismissive and unempathetic. It's essential to have open and honest communication in a relationship, and it seems like you both need to work on finding a better balance and understanding of each other's needs and expectations. 

Your mom's intervention, although possibly biased, highlights that you may have been unreasonable in your expectations. It's essential to take a step back, reflect on your actions, and consider your boyfriend's perspective to work towards a more harmonious and respectful relationship.
